Google Expands Financial Services Verification Program to the United States and Canada

2026-10-27 · GlobalTech Daily Editorial Desk · Source: blog.google

Original conceptual editorial illustration.

Introduction and Key Takeaways

Google has announced the expansion of its Financial Services Verification program to the United States and Canada, slated to begin enforcement in early 2027. Building on safeguards that already cover 2 billion internet users globally across 42 countries, the program aims to protect consumers from online financial scams and brand impersonation. Advertisers will be required to prove they are authorized by official regulators before running financial ads.

What Happened

Google stated that it is bringing its Financial Services Verification program to the U.S. and Canada. The rollout is planned to begin in early 2027. Prior to this expansion, Google pioneered this type of verification starting in the United Kingdom in 2021 and subsequently expanding across the European Union. Currently, more than 97% of the ads people see on Google in the U.S. and Canada already come from identity-verified advertisers.

Key Details of the Verification Process

Under the new policy, financial advertisers must demonstrate that they are authorized by relevant regulators or recognized registries before they can serve certain financial ads. This specialized check works on top of Google's longstanding identity verification framework. Furthermore, Google is partnering with industry groups for verification: in the U.S., Google is working with the American Bankers Association to use its dedicated registry to verify authorized banks, and in Canada, Google is engaging closely with the Canadian Bankers Association.

Role of AI and Multi-Layered Safety Systems

Upfront advertiser verification operates alongside Google's broader safety systems. According to the source, Gemini helped Google's systems catch over 99% of policy-violating ads in 2025 before they were ever served, blocking bad ads in real time. Additionally, Google participates in the Global Signal Exchange, sharing information across the technology, finance, and law enforcement sectors to help stop fraud.

Implementation and Practical Implications

Because regulations differ across borders, Google is adapting its approach for each country through a phased implementation. Ahead of the early 2027 rollout, Google will provide country-specific information for advertisers detailing accepted registries, required credentials, and onboarding instructions. Businesses will be notified if and when they need to complete the process, ensuring they receive clear guidance and preparation time before policy enforcement begins.
